title: Space out touching parcels on a running belt before they reach the scanner
instruction: The three parcels on the belt are touching. Space them out on the belt so that each one has at least 5 cm of empty belt in front of it when it reaches the scanner arch. The belt keeps running. Keep each parcel on the belt until it has passed the scanner arch: you may lift one briefly, but only over the belt, and never set it down anywhere else.
context: Barcode tunnels and dimensioners read one parcel at a time and need a clear gap between parcels; parcels that arrive touching are read as one or not at all and are sent to manual handling. Singulation stations open those gaps on a running line before the scanner. Done by: parcel-sorting and induction workers, and singulation robots in distribution centres.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table (1.10 x 1.30 m) whose edges are 65 cm either side of the midpoint between the bases. A straight belt conveyor crosses the table parallel to the line through the bases, its centre line 32 cm in front of them, running from the robot's right to its left at 5 cm/s. Its grey steel bed (18 cm wide, 1.5 cm thick) runs from 62 cm right to 106 cm left of the midpoint; past the table's left edge it stands on a dark steel post to the floor (6 x 4 cm, centred 101 cm left of the midpoint). On the bed lies a dark rubber belt (16 cm wide, 1 cm thick, 2 mm above the bed) over the same length. A grey steel end stop (18 cm wide, 1 cm thick, rising 6 cm above the belt) closes the belt's left end. Three brown corrugated-cardboard parcels (closed boxes, 9 cm long along the belt, 6 cm across it, 5 cm tall, 150 g each) lie on the belt in its middle, square to it, nose to tail and touching (2 mm apart at most); the front parcel's leading face is 5 cm right of the midpoint. A scanner arch stands over the belt 58 cm left of the midpoint: two dark steel posts (2 x 2 cm) on the table, their inner faces 9.5 cm either side of the belt's centre line, carry a dark steel head (23 cm across the belt, 3 cm along it, 3 cm thick) whose underside is 13 cm above the belt; a red line (4 mm wide) across the head's underside, 58 cm left of the midpoint, marks the scan line. The belt starts with the trial, reaching 5 cm/s in 0.5 s, and does not stop.
scoring: Each parcel passes the scanner from the moment its leading face reaches the scan line until its trailing face has left it; only its first pass counts. 0 for the whole trial if, before its pass, any parcel's centre leaves the area over the belt (between its edges and its ends), even for a moment (set on the table, carried out over the table), or it is off the belt (its underside more than 1 cm above the belt's top) for more than 5 s at a time (a lift ends only once the parcel has lain on the belt again for 0.5 s), or it rests on another parcel (its underside within 1 cm of that parcel's top, over it by 1 cm or more both ways) for 0.5 s; lifts over the belt of up to 5 s are allowed. 0 also if any parcel, at any time during its pass, is not lying on the belt (its underside more than 1 cm above or below the belt's top) or reaches over the belt's edge, or if any parcel has not passed by the end of the trial. The gap in front of a parcel is the distance along the belt from the trailing face of the parcel ahead (the one that reached the line before it) to its own leading face, measured twice: when the parcel ahead's trailing face leaves the line and when this parcel's leading face reaches it; the smaller counts. Otherwise 0.5 for each of the two gaps (in front of the second and the third parcel to pass) of 5 cm or more, and 0.25 for each gap of 2.5 cm to 5 cm: 1.0 when both gaps are 5 cm or more (the trial then ends with success 1 s after the last parcel has passed); 0.75, 0.5 or 0.25 otherwise; 0 for parcels passing touching as they started. What happens to a parcel after its pass doesn't change the score, except that a parcel put back in front of the next one shortens that one's gap.
reset_notes: Stop the belt, put the three parcels back nose to tail and touching with the front one's leading face 5 cm right of the midpoint, and start the belt with the trial. Parcels that passed the scanner are waiting against the end stop.
fidelity: The belt is a fixed plate given the belt's velocity each physics step and put back in place, so parcels on it ride by friction as on a real belt and can be set down anywhere; the arms can't slow it. Parcels are rigid boxes with rubber-like friction (1.2/1.0), more than cardboard; they don't slide at the belt's 0.16 m/s² start. 5 cm/s is slower than real lines, to suit the arms. The scanner isn't simulated: gaps come from the parcels' positions.
